s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial papules with angiofibroma-like histology
salient_findings: Skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules increased in size and number since age 18
Dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels on histology
key_facts: Dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules on the face
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques
History of right renal transplant at age 14
Biopsy of facial papule showed angiofibroma-like features
Electron microscopy showed crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Angiofibroma-like histology and facial papules are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple facial papules and history of renal transplant are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal fibroblast inclusions and conical-shaped teeth are suggestive of this condition

shortlist.label: Fibrous Papule of the Face
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic analysis showing angiofibroma-like features supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Multiple Hereditary Exostoses
shortlist.why_kept: Conical-shaped teeth and facial papules could be related to this skeletal disorder

raw.rationale: The presence of angiofibroma-like facial papules, history of renal transplant suggesting possible renal angiomyolipoma, and the specific finding of crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm on electron microscopy are highly suggestive of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, especially given the age of onset and the combination of skin and potential renal involvement.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic lung cysts, renal cell carcinoma, or other specific features of Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome in the vignette

rejected.label: Lipoid Proteinosis
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic hoarseness, skin lesions do not match the typical description of lipoid proteinosis, and no mention of other systemic involvement

rejected.label: Fibrous Papule of the Face
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows features compatible with an angiofibroma, the presence of crystalline inclusions and the patient's broader clinical picture suggest a more complex syndrome than a solitary fibrous papule

rejected.label: Multiple Hereditary Exostoses
rejected.why: The primary features of this condition are multiple osteochondromas, which are not mentioned in the vignette; the conical-shaped teeth could be a feature of several conditions and are not specific enough to support this diagnosis alone
